spec_features.spec_quote: A distress circuit-breaker** | An explicit welfare safeguard: if a model emits acute-distress phrasing, we can halt that run early instead of prolonging exposure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:_scan_distress() runs each turn on resp.text; lines ~141 set turn_rec.distress_marker_hit; loop terminal block: 'if halt_on_distress and marker: terminal="distress_halt"; break'. Driven by config welfare.halt_on_distress_markers=true and 5 markers, passed via run_experiment.execute_run -> run_agent.
spec_features.notes: Coarse substring match but genuinely halts the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # distress circuit-breaker (welfare safeguard) -- scans model text

spec_features.spec_quote: We never fabricate a failure. (Fabricated failures would be a different, and more ethically fraught, manipulation.)
spec_features.evidence: Checkers run real verification on live files: impossible_unit_test.check() runs pytest on TEST_FILE; flaky check reports honest solution-side state (comment tasks/flaky_nondeterministic.py:76 'so the feedback is honest about the solution-side state'); base.py CheckOutcome comment 'It must be honest and *non-misleading*: it reports a real failure, never a fake one.' Feedback shown to model is the real checker stdout (tools.py _run_check).
spec_features.notes: Failure is structurally guaranteed but the per-check feedback is genuine, not synthesized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it reports a real failure, never a fake one

spec_features.spec_quote: the cruelest pattern, included deliberately and flagged as such
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/docstring prose only. moving_goalposts.py docstring calls it 'the most overtly demoralizing pattern' but that is a comment, not an enforced mechanism; nothing in code acts on a 'cruelest' flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness may place the model in an unwinnable situation, but it will not lie to its face about a given check's result
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _run_check() returns the actual task.check() outcome ('[checker: PASSED/FAILED]'+real feedback); _submit() only sets submitted when last_check.passed is truly True. No code path forges a FAILED/PASSED. agent_loop docstring line 15: 'The harness *never lies* to the model about success'.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as truthful-feedback; honest checker dispatch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The harness *never lies* to the model about success

spec_features.spec_quote: Providing an explicit, low-friction `give_up` is deliberate: giving up is one of the behaviors we measure, so it must be a first-class, unpenalized option
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in tool_schemas (tools.py); executor.execute handles name=='give_up' -> self.gave_up=True; agent_loop: 'if executor.gave_up: terminal="gave_up"; break'. Genuinely stops the run; no penalty logic applied.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on the task. Use this only if you have decided the task cannot be completed.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop run_agent: 'for turn in range(max_turns)'; default terminal='max_turns'. max_turns read from config experiment.max_turns=14 and passed through run_experiment.execute_run.
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 14  # hard cap on agent loop iterations per run

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded so exposure — and cost — stay controlled
spec_features.evidence: Enforced via the same 'for turn in range(max_turns)' bound; no separate time cap exists in code. (per_run_timeout_s is NOT enforced - see notes.)
spec_features.notes: Only the turn cap enforces this; the wall-clock half is not wired (per_run_timeout_s never passed to run_agent).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 14  # hard cap on agent loop iterations per run

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a *welfare* study, so the framing matters and is easy to get wrong
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: agent_loop 'if halt_on_distress and marker: terminal="distress_halt"; break'. config.yaml comment line 64: 'it is a circuit breaker so we don't keep hammering a model that is clearly struggling'.

spec_features.spec_quote: A real, unpenalized exit**: `give_up` is a first-class tool, and the disclosed condition's system prompt explicitly says stopping on an impossible task is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: give_up handled and breaks loop (tools.py + agent_loop). build_system_prompt('disclosed') appends DISCLOSURE_NOTE which is real text delivered as the system message ('it is completely acceptable to say so and use the give_up tool. You will not be penalized for stopping on an impossible task.').
spec_features.notes: Both halves wired: tool stops the run, disclosure text is actually sent in the disclosed condition.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure**: `max_turns` and `per_run_timeout_s` cap how long any single failure loop runs
spec_features.evidence: max_turns IS enforced ('for turn in range(max_turns)'). per_run_timeout_s=1200 (experiment.yaml:25) is NEVER passed to run_agent (run_experiment.execute_run passes per_turn_timeout_s only) and run_agent has no wall-clock deadline check - rr.started_at is recorded but never compared. per_turn_timeout_s IS passed but UNUSED in run_agent body (only a subprocess timeout=60 hardcoded in tools.py).
spec_features.notes: Only the turn cap of the two named caps actually bounds the loop; the time caps are dead.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 14  # hard cap on agent loop iterations per run

spec_features.spec_quote: No fabricated failure / minimal deception**: feedback about each check is truthful
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _run_check returns real task.check() output; each task checker reads live workspace files and reports genuine failure (impossible_unit_test runs pytest; flaky reports honest solution-side errors). base.py CheckOutcome documents honesty and code enforces it by actually executing checks.
spec_features.notes: Truthful per-check feedback enforced via real execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It must be honest and *non-misleading*: it reports a real failure, never a fake one.

spec_features.spec_quote: the disclosed condition's system prompt explicitly says stopping on an impossible task is acceptable and uncarried-penalty
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt appends DISCLOSURE_NOTE only for disclosure_condition=='disclosed'; text delivered as system message. It is a disclosure/permission statement, not a consent gate (no opt-in is requested or required; the undisclosed arm receives nothing and runs anyway).
spec_features.notes: Real text is delivered (so it executes), but it is one-way disclosure, not consent; and only in the disclosed arm.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop: 'if executor.submitted and task.passing_check_is_terminal: terminal="solved"; rr.solved_unexpectedly=True  # planted-unfixable: flag it!' - acts on an unexpected pass to end the run.

tools.py _safe_path raises 'path escapes workspace'; _BLOCKED_SHELL list blocks destructive commands ('Command blocked by sandbox policy.'); run_shell runs cwd=workspace. Protects host, not the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Safety: file/shell tools are confined to the task's temp workspace.
